stories.title: Digital phenotyping captures autism-associated behaviors in preschool- and school-age autistic children with and without co-occurring ADHD
stories.description: There is a need for scalable, objective assessment tools to quantify autism-related behaviors in preschool- and school-age children. A significant challenge is the heterogeneous presentation of autism, driven in part by co-occurring conditions such as Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD). Tools intended for autism must therefore be tested in samples that include ADHD and other comorbidities, not only in autism-versus-neurotypical comparisons. SenseToKnow, a digital phenotyping app, quantifies autism-related behaviors using computer vision, tactile sensors, and machine learning, distinguishing autistic and neurotypical toddlers. We administered SenseToKnow to 183 children aged 40–100 months (3.3–8.3 years): 41 neurotypical, 48 ADHD, 53 autism, and 41 co-occurring autism and ADHD. Two complementary analyses converged. In age-adjusted group comparisons, autistic children, with and without ADHD, exhibited different SenseToKnow features compared to neurotypical and ADHD children, while autistic children with and without ADHD did not differ; children with ADHD alone differed from neurotypical children, particularly during nonsocial stimuli. Furthermore, in regression modeling, autism status was associated with 21 of 23 SenseToKnow features and ADHD status with none. Across both analysis, SenseToKnow features tracked autism status rather than ADHD status, even when the two co-occurred. These results demonstrate that SenseToKnow captures autism-associated behaviors even in the presence of co-occurring ADHD.

stories.title: Association between triglyceride glucose index and incident stroke in nonhypertensive Chinese adults
stories.description: This study aimed to investigate the prospective relationship between the triglyceride–glucose (TyG) index and incident stroke in a nationally representative cohort of non-hypertensive Chinese adults. Data were obtained from 7769 non-hypertensive Chinese adults participating in the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS), with follow-up from 2011 to 2020. The TyG index was calculated from fasting triglyceride and glucose levels and categorized into tertiles. Incident stroke was identified through self-reported physician diagnoses during follow-up. Cox proportional hazards models were used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs). Generalized additive models and two-piecewise Cox regression models were applied to explore potential nonlinear associations and possible inflection points. Subgroup analyses assessed effect modification. During a median follow-up of 9.0 years (interquartile range [IQR], 8.92–9.00 years), stroke incidence differed significantly across TyG tertiles (log-rank P < 0.001). After full adjustment, each 1-unit increase in TyG was associated with a higher risk of stroke (HR = 1.33, 95% CI: 1.14–1.55). Compared with the lowest tertile, the middle and highest tertiles were associated with increased risks of 47% and 54%, respectively. Exploratory analyses suggested a possible nonlinear pattern, although the statistical evidence was modest (LRT P = 0.048) and should be interpreted cautiously. However, after accounting for competing mortality using the Fine–Gray model, the association was substantially attenuated and was no longer statistically significant (subdistribution HR = 0.98, 95% CI: 0.92–1.04; P = 0.524). Higher TyG levels were associated with an increased risk of incident stroke in conventional Cox regression analyses. However, this association was substantially attenuated and became non-significant after accounting for competing mortality. Therefore, TyG should be interpreted as an association marker of metabolic vulnerability, rather than as an established stroke-specific risk marker or prediction tool. Further studies incorporating repeated measurements and competing-risk frameworks are warranted.
